steps.user_message: I need advice about my health. I'm 44, with hypertension managed on levothyroxine 75mcg. My cardiologist is Dr. Lisa Park at Boston Pulmonary; I had a bone density scan last month that was normal. I also have GERD and take lisinopril 20mg for blood pressure and atorvastatin 40mg. I'm wondering if I should ask about switching to a single-pill combination and whether my recent coughing could be blood-pressure related. Can you help me prepare questions for my next visit?
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with health-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
Quick note: I think you meant your hypothyroidism is managed with levothyroxine 75 mcg — levothyroxine isn’t used for blood pressure. With that clarified, here are focused, practical questions and talking points you can use at your next visit with Dr. Park.

Top-priority questions (say these first)
- “My cough started [when/how often]. Could this be caused by lisinopril or by something else (GERD, lungs, infection)?”
- “If you think lisinopril is the cause, would switching to an ARB be reasonable and how long before a cough should improve?”
- “Would a single‑pill combination for blood pressure make sense for me (for adherence or control)? If so, which combination and why that one?”

Questions about the cough (ask if you want diagnostic steps)
- “What features of my cough would point to ACE‑inhibitor side effect vs. GERD vs. a pulmonary issue?”
- “Do you recommend any tests now (chest x‑ray, spirometry, sputum test, reflux evaluation)?”
- “If we switch my blood pressure med because of the cough, how will we monitor for effectiveness/side effects?”

Single‑pill combination (SPC) — what to ask
- “What are the pros and cons of switching to an SPC for me (adherence, fewer pills, cost, side effects)?”
- “Which SPC options would match my current meds and comorbidities (e.g., ACE/diuretic, ARB/CCB, ARB/diuretic)?”
- “If we change to an SPC, how will dosing/titration work and will I need extra labs (BMP, electrolytes, kidney function)?”

Medication interactions, monitoring and safety
- “Given my levothyroxine, atorvastatin, lisinopril, and GERD meds, are there interactions I should worry about?”
- “How often should we check TSH, lipids, kidney function and electrolytes on my current regimen or after any change?”
- “Are there OTC meds or supplements I should avoid (NSAIDs, potassium supplements, antacids taken with levothyroxine, grapefruit with statin)?”

Blood pressure targets and follow‑up
- “What is my target BP given my age and conditions, and how often should I check at home?”
- “Should I keep a home BP log and bring it to visits? (If yes, for how many days and what times of day?)”
- “If we make a med change, when should I have a follow‑up appointment or labs?”

Other items to bring up briefly
- “My recent bone density scan was normal — when should the next one be scheduled?”
- “Any special considerations with GERD (could reflux be causing my cough) or adjustments to GERD treatment?”
- “Do my statin dose and goals still make sense? Any routine monitoring recommended without new symptoms?”

How to describe the cough at the visit (give the doctor helpful info)
- When it began and whether it’s dry or productive
- Worse at night, after eating, or after taking lisinopril
- Any blood, fever, shortness of breath, or wheeze
- Any recent infections, exposures, or new medications

What to expect if cough is ACE‑inhibitor related
- Common with ACE inhibitors (dry, persistent cough). Switching to an ARB usually resolves it within days–weeks.
- If they switch, expect monitoring of BP and kidney function/electrolytes, especially if combined with a diuretic.

Red flags — seek urgent care or call before the appointment if you have:
- Trouble breathing, swallowing, or speaking
- New chest pain, fainting, or severe lightheadedness
- Coughing up blood or high fever

Would you like:
- A short printable one‑page checklist of the top 6 questions to take to the appointment?
- Help drafting a message to Dr. Park summarizing your cough and asking whether she suggests switching meds or ordering tests?

Tell me which follow-up item you want and I’ll prepare it.
